name: RAEA (Retrieval-Augmented Embodied Agents)
venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition), pp. 17985-17995, DOI 10.1109/CVPR52733.2024.01703. Preprint: arXiv:2404.11699 (v1, 17 Apr 2024). Subject: cs.RO.
authors_affiliation: Yichen Zhu, Zhicai Ou, Xiaofeng Mou, Jian Tang (corresponding). Affiliation: Midea Group, AI Lab. Contact: {zhuyc25, zhicai.ou, mouxf, jiantang22}@midea.com.
code_url: N/A - no official code release found. The arXiv page lists generic code-finder integrations (CatalyzeX / Papers with Code) but no authors' repository; the CVPR poster page provides only the PDF/supplementary, no code link. [uncertain]
maintained_repo_url: N/A - not a survey/benchmark; no maintained leaderboard or paper list. RAEA is listed (as an entry) in third-party trackers such as github.com/HCPLab-SYSU/Embodied_AI_Paper_List, but the authors maintain no repo.
task_domain: Embodied / robotic manipulation (decision-making via behavior cloning). RAEA is a vision-(language/audio)-action policy that maps multi-modal observations + instructions to continuous low-level robot actions for manipulation tasks (pick-and-place, contact-rich tasks). Not QA/tool-use/web; it is embodied manipulation policy learning.
problem_setting: Offline, supervised, single-agent imitation learning (behavior cloning) for robotic manipulation in low-data / few-shot regimes (10 or 25 demonstrations per task). A policy network is TRAINED to predict continuous actions; an external policy memory bank (Open X-Embodiment, large-scale cross-embodiment robot trajectories) is queried at both TRAINING and TEST time to supply analogous policies as contextual examples. The memory bank is a fixed, pre-collected external corpus (the authors explicitly ensure it contains NO data from the train/test datasets to avoid leakage). 'Shared memory' means cross-embodiment knowledge shared into the agent, not multi-agent cooperation. Supervision: human-collected demonstration trajectories with action/proprioception labels; optimized with behavior-cloning MSE loss. Evaluated in 3 simulators (Franka Kitchen, Meta-World, ManiSkill-2) and a real Franka robot (40 tasks, 70 objects, 30 trajectories + 5 instructions each).
what_is_retrieved: Policies (multi-modal robot experience tuples). Each retrieved policy m = {instruction i, observation o, action a, proprioceptive state p} drawn from the external policy memory bank; i.e. demonstration trajectory fragments / video segments with their actions and robot states, used as analogous in-context examples for the current task.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus. The policy memory bank is a fixed, pre-collected large-scale robotic dataset (Open X-Embodiment) of cross-embodiment trajectories. It is NOT a growing/episodic memory the agent writes to during deployment; there is no write-back. The agent only reads from this static store at train and test time.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking with a diversity/precision filter. The retriever performs Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) to produce a ranked candidate list and selects the final k policies (generator processes up to K=9 status entries; exact k for retrieved policies not pinned, K capped at 9 for action/proprioception entries). It is not a completeness-of-minimal-set objective; rather a relevance top-k augmented by a redundancy filter (skip candidates whose relevance score is too similar, e.g. >0.9) to ensure diversity. [uncertain on exact retrieved-policy count k]
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: no, Retain: no]. Retrieve: dense multi-modal retrieval of analogous policies from the bank. Reuse: retrieved policies are fed as contextual examples into the policy generator via cross-attention to inform action prediction. Revise: no per-case adaptation/revision step. Retain: no write-back of new experiences to the (static) memory bank.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed as retrieval-augmented generation / retrieval-augmented models (RAG, DPR, MuRAG, Re-Imagen, RA-CLIP, REACT) extended to robotics, and likened to in-context learning. It nonetheless realizes Retrieve+Reuse mechanisms (analogous past experiences used to solve new tasks) under the RAG framing.
retrieval_unit: Full multi-modal policy tuple m = {instruction, observation, action, proprioception} - effectively a demonstration / (sub-)trajectory fragment (the authors note the action bank comprises fragments of videos). So the unit is a single demonstration / trajectory-fragment carrying its action and proprioceptive-state labels, not a token, document, tool-API, or KG-subgraph.
index_source: Static external corpus, offline-collected. The retrievable store is the recently open-sourced Open X-Embodiment (Padalkar et al. 2023), a large-scale cross-embodiment robotic dataset compiled offline from many labs. It is fixed (not induced online, not grown at test time). The authors curate it to exclude the train/test datasets to prevent leakage.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index. All modalities are mapped by a shared mixed-modal encoder (ImageBind) into a unified latent embedding space; retrieval is Maximum Inner Product Search over this flat vector space. No graph/hierarchical/cluster topology; entries are split into instruction vs observation segments but the index itself is a flat embedding store.
retriever_type: Dense bi-encoder retriever (off-the-shelf encoders). Follows DPR-style bi-encoder r(q,m)=E_Q(q)^T E_M(m); E_Q encodes the query, E_M encodes memory policies; both are mixed-modal encoders built on ImageBind (one embedding space binding six modalities). Per-modality features are projected to a common feature plane, averaged, and L2-normalized; similarity via inner product (MIPS). Not BM25, not generative-tool-as-token, not LLM-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / frozen). The retriever uses pre-trained, off-the-shelf multi-modal encoders (ImageBind; CLIP/T5 mentioned as alternatives) without contrastive fine-tuning on similarity labels, LM-feedback, preference, or RL. Retrieval relevance is computed directly from the frozen embedding inner products; no retriever training signal is described. (The downstream policy generator is trained with behavior-cloning MSE loss, but the retriever itself is not trained.)
query_construction: Raw multi-modal input is used as the query q (the instruction-observation pair x), split into an instruction segment (text/audio) and an observation segment (image/video/point cloud), each encoded and fused. A diversity-promoting query perturbation is applied: random token dropout of ~70% of query tokens during retrieval as a regularization mechanism. No semantic query rewriting/decomposition or synthetic-query expansion.
query_granularity: Mixed: task-level at frame onset, then step/observation-level within a frame. Typically an instruction-observation pair is used at the onset of a frame, then retrieval relies solely on the observation for the remainder of the frame until the next user interaction - i.e. a one-shot instruction+observation query followed by repeated observation-conditioned queries during execution.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative on a fixed schedule tied to perception, not learned/active. An instruction-observation query is issued at the onset of each frame; thereafter observation-only retrieval continues per frame until the next user interaction. Retrieval supports real-time correction. Not uncertainty-triggered, not a learned router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule keyed to input frames / user interactions. Retrieval is triggered (a) by a new instruction-observation pair at the start of a frame and (b) by ongoing observations within the frame; the schedule is determined by the perception stream and user-interaction boundaries, not by token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, a learned complexity classifier, or reflection tokens.
reranking: No dedicated rerank stage. After MIPS produces the ranked candidate list, candidates are ordered by relevance score and a redundancy/diversity filter is applied (skip a candidate whose relevance score is too closely aligned, e.g. >0.9, with the query or with already-retrieved policies). This is a similarity-threshold de-duplication / diversity gate rather than a cross-encoder/RRF/instruction-tuned reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Diversity filtering / de-duplication: drop near-duplicate candidates (relevance score >0.9 with query or prior picks) to avoid redundant policies that hurt the generator; plus query-side random token dropout (~70%) as regularization. Within the generator, retrieved-policy tokens are down-sampled/aggregated by an MLP (SC) before cross-attention. No reason-in-documents distillation, decompose-recompose, or compression of content beyond this.
tool_document_engineering: N/A - RAEA retrieves robot policies/demonstrations, not tool/API documents; no tool descriptions are indexed or engineered.
index_content_separation: No explicit progressive-disclosure / index-then-content separation. The same ImageBind embeddings index the policies and the policy generator REUSES the retriever's instruction/observation feature representations (avoiding ~95% redundant recomputation), but heavy content (actions, proprioception) is encoded by separate MLP encoders and loaded together rather than via a lightweight-index-then-fetch protocol. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - not a tool-retrieval system; the policy memory bank is a static dataset with no live tool index, RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling protocol, or CRUD sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling; RAEA does not retrieve tools/APIs.
how_retrieved_used: Training-signal-side prompt augmentation via cross-attention (latent context injection into a trained policy). The policy generator first encodes each retrieved policy's observation, instruction, action, and proprioception into tokens (reusing retriever features; action/proprioception via MLP encoders, with a max of 9 entries each, state/policy delimiter tokens, absolute position embeddings), concatenates them by relevance score, and integrates them into the main policy network through a cross-attention module where retrieved-policy features form the query/key and the current input forms the value. The fused representation drives continuous action prediction, trained end-to-end by behavior cloning (MSE). Retrieved policies thus act as contextual examples (in-context-learning-like) baked into a trained model rather than text prepended to an LLM prompt.
planning_integration: No explicit planner/search. RAEA is a reactive retrieval-augmented policy: retrieve-then-act at each frame. Retrieved analogous policies are injected as one-shot-at-frame-onset contextual exemplars (then observation-conditioned) and fused via cross-attention to produce the next continuous action. There is no multi-step plan, MCTS/tree search, hierarchical subtask decomposition, or plan-then-retrieve loop; it is per-frame retrieve-then-predict-action.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-action / per-frame (per-step within a rollout). Retrieval and action prediction are interleaved at the granularity of perception frames within a rollout (instruction+observation at frame onset, observation-only thereafter), not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call (there is no chain-of-thought; it is a continuous-control policy).
adaptation_mechanism: No CBR-style case revision. Retrieved policies are used essentially as verbatim contextual exemplars whose features are integrated through cross-attention into a trained policy network (a learned latent fusion), rather than being explicitly adapted/edited per case, revised by execution feedback, or critic-guided. Closest to verbatim ICL exemplar + learned latent integration.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected = raw multi-modal demonstration tuple (instruction, observation, action, proprioception) tokenized into latent tokens (observation/instruction features reused from ImageBind retriever; action & proprioception via MLP encoders) and fused via cross-attention. So it is raw-trajectory-fragment content converted into latent/soft tokens, not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, or executable program.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw demonstration / trajectory-fragment (low abstraction). Retrieved units are concrete past robot experiences (single analogous demonstrations / video fragments with their actions and states), not distilled strategies, state-aware guidelines, reusable workflows, or procedural skills.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Diversity/redundancy control plus query regularization rather than a relevance evaluator. (1) Skip near-duplicate candidates (relevance >0.9) so redundant/low-information policies do not dominate; (2) random token dropout (~70%) of the query during retrieval as a regularization mechanism that empirically improves the generator; (3) including cross-embodiment (different-robot) data is found to still aid learning. No retriever-aware SFT, self-reflection relevance check, or reason-in-documents distillation.
memory_type: External static knowledge store (cross-embodiment demonstration corpus) used as shared memory; effectively episodic-demonstration memory but READ-ONLY (not skill-library/workflow/graph/latent, and not agent-written). In the survey's taxonomy: a static external policy/experience corpus rather than a growing episodic memory.
write_back: False (boolean: no). RAEA only reads from the fixed external policy memory bank (Open X-Embodiment); it does not store new experiences/cases/skills back into memory during training or deployment.
online_growth: False. The retrievable store is frozen (offline-collected Open X-Embodiment, curated to exclude train/test data). It does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: Never - no write event occurs; the memory bank is static and read-only.
failure_experience_usage: Not used / not applicable. The static corpus consists of (largely successful) demonstration trajectories; the method does not explicitly store or contrast FAILED/negative experiences, nor mine corrective rules from failures. Retrieval is success-demonstration-only by virtue of the demonstration dataset.
memory_evolution_update: None (append-only is not even applicable) - stored entries are never mutated, merged, pruned, or refined; the external bank is fixed throughout.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is a fixed off-the-shelf dense-similarity top-k (MIPS over frozen ImageBind embeddings) plus a heuristic diversity filter and query token-dropout. It is NOT an RL/soft-Q/M-MDP-learned retrieval policy; the retriever is not trained.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes, cross-EMBODIMENT shared memory (not multi-agent cooperation). RAEA's central idea is 'shared memory' that lets a robot tap collective experiences from MANY different robot embodiments (Open X-Embodiment). An ablation (Table 4) shows multi-embodiment data (success rate 54) beats Franka-only data (48). This is sharing of experience across heterogeneous robot platforms feeding a single agent, not memory shared among multiple concurrently-running agents.
benchmarks: Simulation: Franka Kitchen (Gupta et al.), Meta-World (Yu et al. 2020), ManiSkill-2 (Gu et al. 2023, six rigid- and soft-body tasks: PickCube, StackCube, PickSingleYCB, Fill, Hang, Excavate). Real robot: a self-collected Franka dataset of 40 tasks, 70 objects, 30 human trajectories/task, 5 instructions/task. Policy memory bank: Open X-Embodiment (cross-embodiment).
benchmark_family: Embodied / robotic manipulation (Franka Kitchen / Meta-World / ManiSkill-2 + real Franka). Outside the survey's named embodied set (ALFWorld/ScienceWorld/VirtualHome/Minecraft); it is the real-robot-manipulation branch of the embodied family.
baselines: Franka Kitchen & Meta-World: R3M (Nair et al. 2022, universal visual representation), BLIP-2 (Li et al. 2023, vision-language model), EmbodiedGPT (Mu et al. 2023, embodied VLM), under 10- and 25-demonstration few-shot settings. ManiSkill-2: ResNet152 (He et al. 2016) and Swin-Base (Liu et al. 2021) (both ImageNet-pretrained), with PointNet (Qi et al. 2017) fusion for the point-cloud + image setting.
key_metrics: Mean success rate (%) of the behavior-cloning policy. Simulation: 30 rollouts; 100 randomized trials across 5 tasks per benchmark, 5 runs x 2 camera views, averaged. Real robot: mean success rate over 10 trials per task.
headline_result: RAEA consistently outperforms baselines, most strongly in low-data (10-demo) regimes. On ManiSkill-2 (image+point-cloud setting, Table 1) RAEA achieves PickCube 62.7, StackCube 91.0, PickSingleYCB 43.8, Fill 71.7, Hang 88.1, Excavate 24.0 - beating ResNet152+PointNet (56.6/90.7/28.4/46.9/85.7/18.4) and Swin-Base+PointNet (44.0/90.1/30.6/45.5/86.4/17.0) across all tasks; in the image-only setting RAEA (56.7/93.6/40.2/63.8/87.1/22.4) likewise tops ResNet152 and Swin-Base. On the real Franka robot, full RAEA reaches 54% success (text+image), rising to 69% with image+video+text instruction. On Franka Kitchen and Meta-World RAEA surpasses R3M, BLIP-2, and EmbodiedGPT (Figs 5-6) especially at 10 demonstrations.
ablations: (1) Modality combination, real robot (Table 2): success rises with more modalities - Text/Image 54; Text+Audio/Image 56; Text+Audio/Image+PointCloud 65; Image/Image 58; Image+Video/Image 63; Image+Video/Image+Video 64; Image+Video+Text/Image 69 (language+visual instruction lifts 63->69; adding point cloud lifts 56->65). (2) Status information in retrieved policy (Table 3, text-image): All 54; w/o Proprioception 39; w/o Action & Proprioception 36 - action+proprioception are critical (54->36). (3) Memory-bank embodiment diversity (Table 4): All embodiments 54 vs Franka-only 48 - cross-embodiment data helps. (4) Design choices in retrieval strategy: diversity filtering (skip relevance >0.9) and ~70% random query token dropout both improve generator performance (described qualitatively).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task success rate is reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately. Retrieval quality is assessed indirectly through ablations (modality, status, embodiment diversity) on downstream success rate.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome only (final manipulation success rate). No intermediate process metrics (reasoning faithfulness, step-wise retrieval accuracy, trajectory quality) are reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is addressed mainly via feature reuse: the policy generator reuses the retriever's instruction/observation feature representations, avoiding redundant computation that would otherwise constitute over 95% of the total. Data efficiency is a headline benefit (strong few-shot performance at 10 demos). No retrieval-call counts, latency/speedup numbers, API costs, or token-budget figures are reported. [uncertain on absolute compute/latency]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k with capacity caps. A fixed top-k set of retrieved policies M=(m1..mK) is selected after MIPS and diversity filtering; within each policy the action and proprioception entries are capped at a maximum of 9 each (with state/policy delimiter tokens and absolute position embeddings). No explicit token-budget cap is stated; selection is relevance-ranked then diversity-filtered. [uncertain on exact number of retrieved policies k]
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - RAEA is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Real-robot dataset is self-constructed: 40 tasks (from simple pick-and-place to contact-rich tasks like 'open the drawer and put the pen inside' and 'sort the cube with the same color'), 70 objects, 30 human-collected trajectories per task, 5 distinct instruction annotations per task, on a Franka setup. Outcomes are success/failure of manipulation (physically verifiable). Difficulty signaled by best-system (RAEA) real-robot success of 54% (text-image) up to 69% (multi-modal). Simulation uses existing benchmarks (Franka Kitchen, Meta-World, ManiSkill-2).
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation / dense retrieval lineage: DPR (Karpukhin et al. 2020, bi-encoder), MuRAG (Chen et al. 2022), Re-Imagen (Chen et al. 2022), RA-CLIP (Xie et al. 2023), REACT (Liu et al. 2023, retrieval-augmented customized vision models), retrieval-augmented multimodal LM (Yasunaga et al. 2023). Encoders: ImageBind (Girdhar et al. 2023). Robotics data/policy backbone: Open X-Embodiment / RT-X (Padalkar et al. 2023), R3M (Nair et al. 2022). Evaluation environments: Franka Kitchen, Meta-World (Yu et al. 2020), ManiSkill-2 (Gu et al. 2023). Trained via behavior cloning.
contrasts_with: Prior retrieval-augmented models confined to language/vision/multimodal generation (Re-Imagen, MuRAG, RA-CLIP, REACT) - RAEA instead retrieves robot POLICIES (executed analogous scenarios) for robotic action prediction. Also contrasts with foundation-model embodied agents that store knowledge implicitly in parameters and need extensive training data (R3M, BLIP-2, EmbodiedGPT, RT-1/RT-2-style models) - RAEA augments policy learning with an explicit external cross-embodiment memory, improving low-data generalization without scaling parameters/data.
lineage: Group F (decision/memory/RL) - retrieval-augmented embodied decision-making. Lineage: text RAG / dense retrieval (DPR) -> multimodal RAG (MuRAG, Re-Imagen, RA-CLIP, REACT) -> RAEA, which transfers retrieval augmentation to robotic policy learning by retrieving cross-embodiment demonstration policies from a static external bank (Open X-Embodiment) and fusing them via cross-attention into a behavior-cloned manipulation policy. Distinct from experience/case agents (Optimus-1, ExpeL, JARVIS-1) in that its memory is a fixed read-only external corpus with no write-back or online growth.
